capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Hyundai lists 63.0 kWh for the 2025 Standard Range; 2027 is the same generation with no pack change reported.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: European listing of the same 63 kWh pack (MY24): 60.0 kWh usable (EVKX says 59 net). Pack is shared across markets.

chemistry.notes: EV Database: NMC cathode, pouch (63 kWh pack).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 520 V nominal, 800 V architecture; ArenaEV also says 800 V.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: the US 2026 IONIQ 5 owner's manual (NE1a) describes manual plus navigation-automatic Battery Conditioning; the 2027 car is the same 2025-refresh generation (Electrek 2026-11-11 reports no 2027 charging changes). Years compared: 2025, 2026, 2027.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: no North American page states a peak for the 63 kWh pack. Same pack in Europe: ArenaEV lists 180 kW (CCS, read), EV Database 195 kW (read). Conflicting US evidence: Electrek (US first drive) gives 257 kW and 20 min 10-80% on a 250 kW+ CCS charger without separating the 63 kWh pack (257 kW is the 84 kWh peak). 180 kW (ArenaEV) is recorded; EV Database's 195 kW is higher, so the true peak is uncertain; flag for owner review.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: the US 2026 IONIQ 5 page gives 10.9 kW home charging; EV Database lists the same 11 kW onboard charger for the 63 kWh and 84 kWh cars, so the charger carries over. Source is a US page; no Canadian page states the onboard charger, so Canadian cars on this powertrain (2025-2026) rely on the same carry-over.
